channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Building Clockwork: An AI-Native 2D Game Engine Verified End-to-End with Kane CLI
item.description: Clockwork packs scene building, behaviors, rules, HUD design and playtesting into one browser app, with Kane CLI driving real Chrome to prove the editor and its games work end to end.

item.title: Godot 4: Image size must match texture's image size.
item.description: When uploading layers into an ImageTextureLayered, any mismatch in size or format silently rejects the upload; this troubleshooting note explains why the error appears and how to track it down.

item.title: I built an unofficial Azur Promilia wiki with launch-day tools — here's the data model
item.description: A game launched worldwide today and its player-made wiki went live the same morning — here is how the site's launch-day tools and data model were built.

item.title: One rules engine, two languages
item.description: Shows how CheX implements the chess rules engine twice — TypeScript in the browser and Rust on the server — and keeps both in exact agreement on every move, capture, and checkmate.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 launch boosts Call of Duty HQ to top of Newzoo's PC revenue charts
item.description: The Modern Warfare 4 launch pushed Call of Duty HQ to the top of Newzoo's PC revenue chart, in a month with almost no other major releases.

item.title: Cheese Roll Game - Building a Fast 3D Browser Arcade Downhill Runner
item.description: The author shares how they built a fast, high-performance 3D browser arcade downhill runner with Three.js, covering optimization and game feel.

item.title: The MARROW Project
item.description: A developer is building a game engine called MARROW from scratch to learn how engines work under the hood, with plans to use it for an open-world game later.

item.title: Retention Without a Store: Daily Rewards, Lucky Spin and Boosters Done Kindly
item.description: Using a store-free casual game as an example, this piece shows how daily rewards, lucky spins and boosters can retain players without any purchases — a reference for gentle retention design.

item.title: Turn Raw AI Video Clips into Foot-Anchored Transparent 2D Game Sprites (Godot 4 & Phaser 3)
item.description: While shipping a martial-arts roguelike, the author worked out a pipeline for turning raw AI video clips into foot-anchored, transparent 2D game sprites for Godot 4 and Phaser 3.

item.title: SEO for browser games: 9 fixes to get HTML5 games indexed
item.description: HTML5 game pages are mostly a canvas and a loading bar, so search engines find little to index — here are nine fixes to get browser games discovered.

item.title: Designing Environments That Tell a Story for 007 First Light
item.description: Environment artist Thomas Pulluelo shares how he built atmospheric spaces for the new James Bond game that subtly guide players through gameplay.

item.title: First Week for an Outstaffed Game Developer in India: A Repo, Build and Review Checklist
item.description: When a studio brings an outstaffed developer into its own team, the first week's repo access, build setup and review process decide whether the arrangement works — this checklist covers the engineering side.

item.title: Ziva VFX-Inspired Physics-Based Muscle Simulation Tool For 3ds Max, Maya, Blender & Houdini
item.description: HézFX brings muscle, fascia, fat, and skin into one unified simulation, giving animated characters a more believable sense of flesh in motion.

item.title: How Hyperscales was built, part 1: We woke it up - the audit and what we found
item.description: The first devlog in a series on rescuing a half-forgotten prototype into a presentable game in two days, starting with what the code audit uncovered.

item.title: Hire an Unreal Engine Developer: Costs and Options
item.description: The article compares the costs of hiring Unreal Engine developers as freelancers, through agencies or studios, or as full-time employees, helping small teams budget the hire.

item.title: Isometric Warsaw turns open city data into a playful Three.js map
item.description: This Three.js project turns open city data into a playful pixel-art isometric map of Warsaw, explaining the choices behind its look, navigation and flight mode.

item.title: Unity & Unreal Change The Way You Access Assets
item.description: The latest Unity and Unreal releases both overhaul how developers access assets — Unity's new Asset Library plugin reworks the Asset Store flow — so check how your workflow is affected.

item.title: Closing the Loop: How Clockwork's Built-in AI Agent Uses Kane CLI to Verify the Games It Builds
item.description: Clockwork's built-in agent doesn't trust its own word that it "added coins" — it has Kane CLI play the result in a real browser and return a typed verdict, a model for end-to-end verification of AI-built games.

item.title: Recreating the Scale Model Look of a Rally Diorama in Houdini
item.description: Will Hoskin walks through recreating the look of a handmade rally diorama in 3D, using Houdini's procedural tools to craft cotton dust, wire trees, and plastic figures.

item.title: Turning Whimsical 2D Town Into Cozy 3D World
item.description: Pedro Henrique Placido Silva explains how he turned a charming fantasy town from a 2D illustration into a 3D scene, covering modeling, texturing, vegetation, and the final render.
